## Problem Statement

New users face a blank platform: the first workbench, first pipeline, and first
model deployment all start from empty forms, and time-to-first-success is
measured in days. We want a curated tutorial gallery in the Dashboard — a set
of maintained, tested tutorials (notebooks and pipelines) that users can launch
into their own project with one click. This requires product code (the gallery
and launch mechanics), authored content (the tutorials themselves), and
documentation — three different kinds of work with different owners and review
processes.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook, or importing the pipeline). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Six curated tutorials exist covering the core journeys: first workbench, data prep, first training run, first pipeline, first deployment, first RAG app. Each is tested against the current release. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution process for new tutorials. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Notebooks
- Data Science Pipelines
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Partner- or community-contributed tutorial intake (contribution process is
  documented, but no submission tooling this release)
- Localization of tutorial content

## Open Questions

None.

# Tutorial packaging format: metadata, pinned images, and validation manifest

## Description

Defines the packaging format that makes each tutorial a versioned, independently
testable artifact: a metadata description of the tutorial, pinned references to
the images it runs against, and a validation manifest capturing how the tutorial
is certified against a platform release. The format is the contract between
authored tutorial content and the Dashboard gallery that launches it, so
tutorials can be added, versioned, and validated without Dashboard releases.

## Scope

- Define the tutorial metadata that describes a packaged tutorial (identity,
  core journey, presentation information) and is consumable by the tutorial
  gallery
- Define the image-pinning rules: each packaged tutorial records the exact
  image references (workbench image and any other images it requires) it runs
  against
- Define the validation manifest: the checks a tutorial must pass to be
  certified against a given platform release
- Provide the validation tooling that executes a packaged tutorial's validation
  manifest and reports pass/fail results
- Deliver the format as a documented specification together with one reference
  tutorial packaged in the format. The reference tutorial is a minimal exemplar
  that serves as the format's test fixture only — it is not a curated tutorial
  and must not grow into substantive content; authoring the curated tutorial
  set is a separate content-authoring deliverable outside this epic

## Acceptance Criteria

- The packaging format specification defines all three constituents stated in
  the strategy: metadata, pinned images, and a validation manifest
- A minimal reference tutorial is packaged in the format and its validation
  manifest executes via the validation tooling with a deterministic pass/fail
  result
- Every image reference in a packaged tutorial is pinned to an exact reference
  at packaging time
- Packaging and validating a new or updated tutorial requires no change to the
  Dashboard — tutorials are versioned and testable independently of Dashboard
  releases

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1) — full coverage: the tutorial packaging format, its metadata,
  pinned images, and validation manifest, enabling versioned and independently
  testable tutorials

# Author and test six curated getting-started tutorials

## Description

Authors the six curated tutorials covering the core platform journeys — first
workbench, data prep, first training run, first pipeline, first deployment, and
first RAG app — as notebook-based and pipeline-based content, each packaged in
the tutorial packaging format and tested against the current platform release.
These are the tutorials the Dashboard gallery launches into a user's project.

## Scope

- Author tutorial content for the six core journeys: first workbench, data
  prep, first training run, first pipeline, first deployment, first RAG app
  (notebooks for the notebook-based journeys, pipeline definitions for the
  pipeline journey)
- Package each tutorial per the tutorial packaging format: metadata, pinned
  images, and a validation manifest
- Run each tutorial's validation manifest against the current platform release
  and fix content until every tutorial passes
- Validate the notebook tutorials end to end in a workbench in a user project
  (the tutorial notebook opens and runs in a spawned workbench)
- Keep tutorial content maintained: record the release each tutorial is
  certified against

## Acceptance Criteria

- Six curated tutorials exist, one per core journey listed in the strategy
- Each tutorial is packaged with its metadata, pinned images, and validation
  manifest per the packaging format
- Each tutorial passes its validation manifest against the current platform
  release (measured by the validation tooling's pass result for every tutorial)
- Each notebook-based tutorial opens and runs to its success state in a
  workbench in a fresh user project

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0) — full coverage: six curated, release-tested tutorials across the
  core journeys
- HLR-1 (P0) — contributes the curated tutorial set that the Dashboard
  tutorial gallery launches

# Dashboard tutorial gallery with one-click launch into projects

## Description

Adds the tutorial gallery to the Dashboard: a curated, browsable set of
getting-started tutorials from which a user launches a tutorial into their own
project with one click — opening a workbench preloaded with the tutorial
notebook, or importing the tutorial pipeline into the project. The gallery
renders and launches tutorials purely from their packaged artifacts, so curated
content can be added or updated without Dashboard releases.

## Scope

- New tutorial gallery surface in the Dashboard presenting the curated
  tutorials and their metadata to the user
- One-click launch mechanics for a notebook tutorial: open a workbench in the
  user's project running the tutorial's pinned image with the tutorial
  notebook loaded
- One-click launch mechanics for a pipeline tutorial: import the tutorial
  pipeline into the user's project's Data Science Pipelines application
- Gallery consumption of the tutorial packaging format: browse from tutorial
  metadata, launch from pinned image references, so adding or updating a
  tutorial requires no Dashboard code change
- Scope guard: this epic delivers the gallery and launch mechanics only —
  tutorial content and its packaging format are produced elsewhere, and no
  tutorial submission/intake tooling is in scope this release

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user can open the tutorial gallery in the Dashboard and browse the curated
  tutorials with their metadata
- One-click launch of a notebook tutorial opens a workbench in the user's
  project with the tutorial notebook loaded and running on the tutorial's
  pinned image
- One-click launch of a pipeline tutorial imports that pipeline into the
  user's project
- A packaged tutorial can be added to or updated in the curated set with no
  Dashboard code change (verified by updating a tutorial's packaged content and
  observing the gallery pick it up)
- The end-to-end launch path is verified with a released packaged tutorial:
  launching it from the gallery produces a running workbench / imported
  pipeline in the user's project

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0) — full coverage: the Dashboard tutorial gallery with one-click
  launch of a tutorial into the user's project (workbench with notebook, or
  imported pipeline)

# Validate tutorial pipeline import and execution on Data Science Pipelines

## Description

Validation epic for the Data Science Pipelines surface of the tutorial
gallery's launch path: confirms that the curated pipeline tutorials import and
execute correctly on current-release Data Science Pipelines applications. No
Data Science Pipelines code changes are expected — the deliverable is the
validated pipeline tutorials and a recorded validation result, with any
compatibility defects fed back to the tutorial content or escalated as
platform issues.

## Scope

- Import each packaged pipeline tutorial from the curated set into a
  Data Science Pipelines application in a test project
- Execute each imported pipeline tutorial end to end and record the results
  against the current platform release
- Triage failures: content defects go back to the tutorial content for fixing;
  Data Science Pipelines platform incompatibilities are escalated with
  reproduction details
- Confirm the pipeline tutorials' use of the current KFP v2 API/SDK surface
  remains compatible with the release under validation

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every pipeline-based tutorial in the curated set imports successfully into a
  current-release Data Science Pipelines application in a test project
- Every imported pipeline tutorial executes to completion in that project
- A validation record documents the import and execution result for each
  pipeline tutorial, and every observed defect is filed and triaged (content
  defect or platform issue)

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0) — the pipeline tutorials are tested against the current release
- HLR-1 (P0) — the "importing the pipeline" launch path is validated on the
  Data Science Pipelines surface

# Document tutorial gallery usage and the tutorial contribution process

## Description

Red Hat documentation for the tutorial gallery covering two audiences: end
users who want to find and launch tutorials into their projects, and
contributors who want to add new tutorials to the curated set. Documentation
starts after the implementation work it describes is complete.

## Scope

Content outline:

- Using the tutorial gallery (end-user topic): what the curated tutorials
  cover, how to browse the gallery, and how to launch a tutorial into your
  project — both launch paths (workbench opened with the tutorial notebook,
  and imported pipeline)
- Contributing a tutorial (contributor topic): the contribution process end to
  end — packaging a tutorial in the tutorial packaging format (metadata,
  pinned images, validation manifest), the validation requirements a tutorial
  must pass against a platform release, and how curated tutorials are reviewed
  and published; contribution is a documented process this release, with no
  submission tooling
- Verification pass: every documented step is executed against the implemented
  gallery and a packaged tutorial before publication

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation covers using the tutorial gallery, including both
  launch paths, matching the implemented gallery behavior
- Published documentation covers the tutorial contribution process, including
  the packaging format's requirements and the validation a contributed
  tutorial must pass
- All content is technically reviewed against the implemented gallery and the
  tutorial packaging format (each documented step executed as written)
- The contribution documentation describes the process without referencing any
  submission tooling, which is out of scope this release

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2) — full coverage: documentation of gallery usage and the tutorial
  contribution process

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9019 (Curated getting-started tutorial gallery)

The strategy explicitly spans three kinds of work with different owners and review
processes: product code (the Dashboard gallery and launch mechanics), authored
content (the six curated tutorials), and documentation. It is therefore not
below-threshold and not docs-only; it proceeds through full decomposition.

graph TD

| E001 → E002 | Rule 12 (framework → consumer) | Tutorials are authored, packaged, and validated in the packaging format; content authoring builds against the format definition. |

**Deliberately absent edges:**

## Health Warnings

- **Missing strategy sections (non-blocking):** the strategy has no Impacted Teams
  table, no per-component change descriptions (Affected Components is a bare
  list), no Dependencies table, no Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, and no
  Non-Functional Requirements. Teams were derived from
  `.context/architecture-context/` owning teams; acceptance criteria were derived
  from the HLRs.
- **Team assumptions:** tutorial authoring and the packaging format are assigned
  to the Workbenches team (owning team of the Notebooks component per
  `notebooks.md`). If a dedicated enablement/content team owns tutorial
  authoring, reassign E001/E002. The documentation epic is assigned to a docs
  team ("RHOAI Docs"); the strategy names no docs team and no architecture
  context file exists for the Documentation component.
- **Passive component classification:** Notebooks and Data Science Pipelines are
  treated as passive (no code changes indicated; the launch mechanics use
  existing Notebook and KFP v2 surfaces). Workbench launch validation is folded
  into acceptance criteria on E002/E003 (same owning team as Notebooks content).
  The Data Science Pipelines validation became a separate epic (E004) because a
  different team owns that surface.
- **Out-of-scope consistency:** contribution tooling is out of scope while HLR-4
  asks only for contribution *documentation* — consistent, not a scope trap.
  Submission tooling must not creep into E005's scope.
- **Priority note:** HLR-3 is P1 but E001 is P0 by inheritance (an epic blocking
  all P0 work is implicitly P0). Not an inversion — it reflects the enablement
  chain.
- **E002 size (above guideline, not split):** estimated at ~3 weeks of a single
  author's effort (six heterogeneous journeys across two content formats),
  above the ~2-week guideline. Not split because it is one logical change — a
  single homogeneous content-authoring sweep sharing one packaging/validation
  pipeline and one release-certification loop; splitting by journey count or by
  work type (authoring vs packaging vs testing) would duplicate the shared
  setup and fragment the format's single validation loop. Conditional re-split
  trigger: if, once the first two tutorials are authored and validated, more
  than one week of estimated effort remains for the other four — or if
  separate authors are assigned per journey family — split E002 along the
  notebook-journeys vs pipeline-journeys axis into parallel epics.
- **E001 reference tutorial is a minimal exemplar:** E001 deliberately bundles
